hints: Focus on the neutralisation, since one COOH group means one mole of acid reacts with exactly one mole of NaOH.
Work out moles of NaOH from 25.0 cm3 of 2.0 mol dm-3, this is also the moles of acid present in 4.4 g.
Use mass divided by moles to get the Mr of about 88, then check which empirical formula fits a molecule with one COOH group.
walkthrough:
**Find moles of NaOH used**

Great start, let's turn the titration data into moles. Remember to change cm3 to dm3 first.

$$\text{moles NaOH} = \frac{25.0}{1000} \times 2.0 = 0.050 \text{ mol}$$

**Find moles and Mr of the acid**

The acid has one $\text{COOH}$ group per molecule, so it is monobasic. That means the equation is 1 to 1:
$$\text{RCOOH} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCOONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
So moles of acid = 0.050 mol as well. Now find its relative molecular mass:
$$M_r = \frac{\text{mass}}{\text{moles}} = \frac{4.4}{0.050} = 88$$

**Link Mr to empirical formula**

Now test the empirical masses. $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$ has mass $(2 \times 12) + (4 \times 1) + 16 = 44$. Two units of this gives $44 \times 2 = 88$, which matches perfectly.

That gives molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$, which can be written as $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{COOH}$. It has exactly one COOH group, so everything fits. The empirical formula (simplest ratio) is therefore $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$.

options.A: CH2O has an empirical mass of 30. No whole number multiple of 30 gives Mr = 88, so it cannot be the acid neutralised here.
options.B: C2H4O has empirical mass 44. Since Mr = 88, the molecule contains 2 empirical units, giving C4H8O2. This is a monocarboxylic acid such as butanoic acid, C3H7COOH, with one COOH group. This matches all the data.
options.C: C3H6O3 has empirical mass 90, which is already larger than the measured Mr of 88. It would also imply 3 O atoms, suggesting more than one COOH group.
options.D: C4H8O2 is the molecular formula (Mr = 88), not the empirical formula. It simplifies by dividing by 2 to C2H4O. This is a classic trap confusing molecular with empirical.
